rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All creatures continually declare God's transcendence; the opening recalls the previous surah's account of divine might, urges remembrance, and prepares for resurrection.
rows.anchor: Yukarılarda ve aşağıda bütün mahlûkāt her zaman ve her lahza müstemirren Allah’ı tenzih eder durur.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sovereignty and praise belong only to God because He creates, preserves, and freely disposes of all things.
rows.anchor: Mülk O’nun, hamd O’nundur O’ndan başkasının değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human nature is disposed to belief yet capable of disbelief; the creation of radically opposed groups within one species displays God's power.
rows.anchor: iktizâ etmekle beraber küfre de müsta‘iddir, imana da müsta‘iddir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consequential fa presents belief and disbelief as God's creation while also relating them to human acquisition and choice, thereby warning disbelievers.
rows.anchor: küfür ve iman dahi Allah’ın halk ve takdîri olmakla beraber insanların kesb ü iradesiyle de[^5] alâkadar

rows.speaker: Kādî Beyzâvî
rows.claim: Baydawi stresses that the unbeliever is destined and directed toward disbelief, while the believer is destined for faith and its prompting cause.
rows.anchor: Kādî Beyzâvî daha ziyade birinci noktaya işaretle[^6] şöyle demiş

rows.speaker: Ebussuud
rows.claim: Abu al-Su'ud says people are created with capacities for knowledge and action, but some choose disbelief against their nature and others choose faith; all ought to choose faith in gratitude.
rows.anchor: Ebussuud da ikinci noktaya temas ederek şöyle tefsir etmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rejects both Jabrī denial of human acquisition and Mu'tazilī attribution of creation to humans without God's decree; it indicates both divine creation and human choice.
rows.anchor: hiç kesbi olmayarak mücerred Allah’ın hilkatine nisbet etmek nasıl doğru değilse

rows.speaker: Ebû Zer
rows.claim: Abu Dharr transmits a Prophetic report that an angel visits the embryo after forty days and records its sex and future blessed or wretched state by God's decree.
rows.anchor: Ebû Zer radıyallâhu anh’tan tahric eylemişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine foreknowledge and predestination do not prevent deeds from depending on human choice; even acquired acts are created by God, with faith pleasing and disbelief displeasing to Him.
rows.anchor: bu mukadderâtın böyle min tarafillah bilinip takdir olunması onun bazılarının abdin kesb ü ihtiyârına merbut olmasına mâni‘değildir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moral responsibility concerns acts connected to human effort and choice; acts wholly beyond choice are not imputed as posthumous responsibility, though their worldly effects are endured.
rows.anchor: sırf cebrî olduklarından dolayı uhrevî mes’ûliyet itibariyle bunlar[^19] insana muzâf değildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God created the heavens and earth in truth, not play; His wise ordering assigns consequences justly, never crediting one creature with another's due.
rows.anchor: bütün gökleri ve yeri hak ile halketmiştir beyhûde ve oyuncak olarak değil.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣūrah can mean both bodily shape and intelligible spiritual form; humans have proportionate bodies and souls able to apprehend truth.
rows.anchor: cismânî şekil ve biçime ıtlak olunduğu gibi, ma‘kul olan mânevî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human discernment can distinguish truth from falsehood and good from evil, allowing a person through conduct either to refine the self or degrade it.
rows.anchor: hakkı bâtıldan, güzeli çirkinden, hayrı şerden, tatlıyı acıdan temyiz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human being is described as joining the higher and lower worlds through the divinely commanded spirit and material body.
rows.anchor: İnsan âlem-i ulvî ile âlem-i süflî beynini câmi‘dir. Bu da mücerredât âleminden emr-i rabbânî olan rûhu ile maddiyyât âleminden olan bedeni hasebiyledir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A couplet pictures the human as seemingly small yet containing the greater universe; the author connects this to the Qur'anic subjection of the heavens and earth for people.
rows.anchor: Sanırsın ki sen bir küçük cirimsin

rows.speaker: Ebü’l-Feth-i Büstî
rows.claim: Busti urges people to cultivate the soul's virtues, since their humanity rests in spirit rather than body.
rows.anchor: Yine bu mânadan dolayı Ebü’l-Feth-i Büstî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God created humanity in the best form, people should avoid ugliness, compete in the best deeds, draw near to eternal beauty, and remember their return is to Him.
rows.anchor: insanı en güzel surette yaratmıştır. O hâlde bunun hakkı, lâyıkı ve vecîbesi de insanların çirkin hâllerden sakınıp

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masīr is a mimṣdar meaning return here, while in wa-bi'sa al-maṣīr it is a place noun meaning the destination.
rows.anchor: sayrûret etmek, rücû‘etmek, dönüp gitmek mânasına masdar-ı mîmî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All return to God's just presence, where people are gathered and good and evil are distinguished for fitting recompense in the next life.
rows.anchor: O’nun hiçbir haksızlığa yer vermeyen huzûr-ı ehadiyetinde toplanılıp haklı haksız, iyi ve kötü ayırt edilerek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows everything in heaven and earth, all hidden and public matters, and the full depths of human hearts and actions.
rows.anchor: siz her ne gizliyor ve her ne açıklıyorsanız hepsini bilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should use their beautiful creation and God's gifts well, give thanks, and come before Him without the shame of disbelief and rebellion.
rows.anchor: O’nun yarattığı o güzel hilkati hakkıyla güzel kullanmalı, O’nun nimetlerini yerinde sarfetmeli, hamd ü şükrünü edâ etmeli

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The painful worldly punishments of Noah's, ʿĀd's, Thamūd's, Lot's, and Pharaoh's peoples warn present unbelievers; a more painful punishment awaits them in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: Nûh kavmi, Âd ve Semûd ve kavm-i Lût ve Firavun gibi küfürde ısrar edenlerin küfürlerinin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples were punished because messengers brought clear proofs but they objected that humans could not guide them, disbelieved, and turned away.
rows.anchor: onlara peygamberleri beyyinelerle, açık deliller, mucizelerle geliyorlardı da bunlara karşı o kâfirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God showed that He had no need of their faith or obedience by destroying them; He is self-sufficient from all creation and worthy of praise.
rows.anchor: gösterdi onların ne iman ve tâatlerine ne de kendilerine asla ihtiyâcı bulunmadığını anlattı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghanī means God is independent of the entire universe and can replace it; Ḥamīd means He possesses every perfection and deserves praise.
rows.anchor: Allah Ganî’dir sade onlardan değil, bütün âlemînden ganîdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unbelievers deny resurrection as though death ended everything and deeds had no lasting truth or consequence, reducing people to decaying bodies.
rows.anchor: öldükten sonra her şey yok olur biter, iyilik de kötülük de doğruluk da eğrilik de boşa gider

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is commanded to swear by his Lord that all people, believers and unbelievers alike, will certainly be raised.
rows.anchor: sizler gerek kâfir gerek mü’min bütün insanlar lâbüd ba‘s olunacaksınız

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People will be informed of their deeds and judged; this resurrection and recompense are easy for God, the Creator capable of everything.
rows.anchor: İman edip iyi amel yapanlar kârlı çıkıp bahtiyar olacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People must believe in God, Muhammad, and the revealed light, which the author identifies as the Qur'an, and act according to its guidance.
rows.anchor: yani şuurları, basîretleri tenvir eyleyecek Hak nûru olan Kur’ân’a iman ediniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will gather people for the Day of Gathering, the Day of Mutual Loss, when who gained and who lost becomes clear.
rows.anchor: Sizleri o dernek gününe derleyip toplayacağı gün

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taghābun derives from gabn: losing or deceiving in a transaction or judgment, by selling or buying below or above value; mutual deception becomes manifest.
rows.anchor: alışverişte veya re’yde aldanmak veya aldatmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source distinguishes gabn in commerce, pronounced with a silent bāʾ, from gaban in judgment, with both consonants vocalized.
rows.anchor: re’yde olursa ikisinin de fethiyle

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: Raghib defines gabn as a concealed imbalance in dealings and says the Day of Mutual Loss reveals whether spiritual transactions gained or lost.
rows.anchor: Râgıb der ki: “‘Gabn’, aranızdaki muamelede

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'anic exchanges of selves and wealth for God's pleasure, or of God's covenant for a small price, will have their true profit or loss exposed that day.
rows.anchor: bu alışverişlerde kâr ve zarar hep o zaman anlaşılacaktır.

rows.speaker: some commentators
rows.claim: Some say worldly objects will appear to people on that day in a measure contrary to what they had seemed to possess in life.
rows.anchor: O gün eşyâ onlara dünyadaki mikdarları hilâfına zuhur edecektir

rows.speaker: Bazı müfessirîn
rows.claim: Some exegetes trace gabn to concealment, naming concealed bodily folds magābin and describing a woman as tayyibat al-magābin.
rows.anchor: Bazı müfessirîn de demiştir ki

rows.speaker: Keşşâf
rows.claim: The Kashshaf reads mutual loss as a metaphor from trade: the saved occupy the places the wretched would have occupied, and vice versa.
rows.anchor: Keşşâf da der ki: “Burada

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says each person entering Paradise is shown the place in Hell they would have occupied had they done evil, and each person entering Hell is shown the Paradise place they forfeited.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah’ın hadîsinde de ‘cennete giren her kula

rows.speaker: Mücâhid ve Katâde
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada explain the day as the day when the people of Paradise deceive the people of Hell.
rows.anchor: Mücâhid ve Katâde’den “ehl-i cennetin ehl-i cehennemi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers a definition broad enough to include both reciprocal and one-sided deception: the day real profit and loss are realized.
rows.anchor: Biz buna hakīkī aldatma ve aldanmanın tahakkuk ettiği kâr ve zarar günü demekle her iki ihtimâli de ifade etmiş olacağımız kanaatinde bulunuyoruz.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it mutual loss ironically addresses worldly people consumed by love of wealth who aim to deceive others; only the greatest final gain and loss are truly decisive.
rows.anchor: Dünya mahabbetine dalmış olan bedbahtların en büyük emelleri, ticaret sevdâsıyla şunu bunu aldatmak olduğu cihetle

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever believes in God and does good for that day has sins covered and enters eternal gardens; the greatest triumph is safety and supreme divine pleasure.
rows.anchor: Allah ondan onun kabahatlerini keffâretleyip örtecek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who disbelieve and deny God's signs lose, remain in the Fire, and reach a wretched destination.
rows.anchor: Küfredip bizim âyetlerimize yalan diyenler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author renders the rule as the affluent spending according to their means and the constrained spending from God's provision; no soul is charged beyond what it has received, and hardship is followed by ease.
rows.anchor: Genişliği olan genişliğinden infak etsin, rızkı dar olan da Allah’ın ona verdiğinden infak eylesin. Allah bir nefse verdiğinden başka teklif etmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to testify sincerely for God is directed to witnesses, while the preceding divorce instructions address divorcing husbands.
rows.anchor: Şehadeti de Allah için dosdoğru[^1] edâ edin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The collective address covers both husbands and witnesses and summarizes divorce by the waiting period, observing limits, then retaining or separating graciously and testifying at the right time.
rows.anchor: talâkı iddet gözeterek vermek, iddeti ihsâ etmek, Allah’tan korkup günahtan sakınmak, çıkarıvermemek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These instructions admonish those who believe in God and the Last Day or retain the capacity to believe; darkened, sealed hearts do not heed advice.
rows.anchor: bunlara riayet edip korunarak intifâ‘edecek olanlar Allah’a ve âhirete imanı olan veya iman kābiliyeti silinmemiş bulunan kimselerdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever fears God and avoids disobedience is given a way out of distress, including family hardship, and unexpected provision; both sides in divorce should trust this.
rows.anchor: Allah onun için bir mahrec yaratır onu düştüğü darlıktan ve ezcümle aile yüzünden çekmekte bulunduğu sıkıntılardan kurtulup çıkacağı bir yol

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report about God's opening and unexpected provision offers a way out from worldly doubt, death's distress, and the Day of Judgment's trials.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem bu kavl-i ilâhîyi

rows.speaker: Ebû Zer
rows.claim: Abu Dharr says the Prophet repeated the verse about piety and provision and told him that it would suffice everyone if they followed it.
rows.anchor: Ebû Zer radıyallâhu anh’tan şöyle mervîdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reliance on God means trusting His power through what befalls a person and submitting one's work to His command; then God suffices one's needs.
rows.anchor: her kim Allah’a tevekkül kılarsa başına gelen herhangi bir şeye karşı

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: A report cited through Razi says the person who wants to be strongest should rely on God.
rows.anchor: Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem buyurmuştur ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings His decree to completion regardless of human reliance; hardship and comfort pass, death arrives, and people meet the afterlife with their deeds, while reliance is itself commanded and rewarded.
rows.anchor: Dünyada acı da geçer, tatlı da geçer, sıkıntı da geçer, refah da geçer. Ecel gelince mukadder olan ölüm

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God assigns every thing a measure and limit, within which its course and value are set.
rows.anchor: Hakikat Allah her şey için bir kadr takdir kılmıştır. Bir hadd ü mikdar tahsis buyurmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Causes possess no independent power: fire burns and provision feeds only to the extent God decrees; confidence in causes is limited but confidence in God is not.
rows.anchor: Tesir ve hüküm onun değil, Allah’ındır. Asıl ilm ü kudretine itimad olunacak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Proper trust is active obedience and piety, acknowledging one's shortcoming while leaving the result to God's power, not complacently abandoning effort.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın gösterdiği yolda gücü yettiği kadar vazifeye ihtimam

rows.speaker: Resûlullah
rows.claim: The Prophet's instruction to tie the camel before trusting God illustrates that trust includes taking the prescribed means; the order of piety before trust points to the same lesson.
rows.anchor: Hadîs-i nebevîde a‘râbîye اعْقِلْهَا وَتـَوَ َّكلْ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God measures human conditions, provision, divorce, waiting periods, housing, and maintenance; the decree's universal measure summarizes prior rules and introduces the next.
rows.anchor: Dünyada acı da geçer, tatlı da geçer

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women who have reached customary menopause, estimated at ages fifty-five to sixty, observe a three-month waiting period after divorce.
rows.anchor: ekser âdete nazaran iyâs sinni elli beş ve altmış olarak takdir edilmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase if you are in doubt is a parenthetical response to people asking how to count these periods, not doubt that the women have ceased menstruating.
rows.anchor: burada bu إِنِ ٱرْتَبْتُمْ kaydı ihtirâzî değil, bu meseleyi soranların veya soracak olanların vukū‘bulan veya bulacak olan suallerine nazaran vukū‘îdir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waiting period for such women is three months; if no pregnancy becomes apparent, they may then be retained or released graciously as in the earlier rule.
rows.anchor: onların iddetleri üç aydır. Üç ay beklerler, bu müddet zarfında bir haml tebeyyün etmezse nihâyetinde evvelkiler gibi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women who have not menstruated also wait three months; syntactically this can be a coordinated noun phrase or an independent clause, with the latter better matching an independent legal ruling.
rows.anchor: Mikdarda iştirak itibariyle evvelki ve hükümde istiklâl itibariyle ikinci daha muvâfıktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule includes girls below seventeen who have not reached puberty and women past the maximum puberty age of seventeen who never menstruated; one or two periods do not establish a regular custom.
rows.anchor: on yedi yaşından küçük olup henüz bülûğa ermemiş olduklarından dolayı hayız görmemiş olanlara

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A cycle is established only after at least three occurrences; after three periods followed by ongoing cessation, a woman is called extendedly pure, and her waiting period is difficult.
rows.anchor: âdet muttarid oldukda muteber olur ki ekalli üçtür

rows.speaker: Hanefiyye
rows.claim: The Hanafis say a woman with extended purity follows the waiting period of a menstruating woman until menopause, since she is neither a non-menstruator nor menopausal.
rows.anchor: Hanefiyye bunun hâiz iddetine tâbi‘olarak sinn-i iyâsa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author instead favors waiting only through the longest usual pregnancy term to resolve pregnancy uncertainty, since keeping her longer would conflict with the lawgiver's purpose.
rows.anchor: Âcizâne kanaatim bunda haml şüphesini nazar-ı i‘tibâra alarak müddet-i hamlin ekserine kadar bekletmektir.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pregnant woman's waiting period, whether after divorce or her husband's death, ends upon delivery, even for an early-stage embryo; twins require waiting for the later birth.
rows.anchor: Mudğa veya aleka hâlinde bir sıkt bile olsa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although widows ordinarily wait four months and ten days, this verse states without qualification that a pregnant woman's period ends at delivery.
rows.anchor: hâmil olanların iddeti vaz‘-ı hamle kadar olduğu

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali ve İbn Abbas
rows.claim: A reported view restricts this verse to divorced women but requires pregnant widows to wait whichever is longer: four months and ten days or delivery; the Imāmī Shīʿa adopt it.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali ve İbn Abbas bu âyetin mutallakalar hakkında olduğuna zâhib olmuşlar

rows.speaker: İbn Abbas ve Ebû Seleme
rows.claim: In the report of a widow delivering forty days after her husband's death, Ibn Abbas says to wait the longer period, while Abu Salama says delivery makes her lawful; Abu Hurayra sides with Abu Salama and Umm Salama cites the case of Subayʿa.
rows.anchor: İbn Abbas ‘âhir-i eceleyn’ dedi

rows.speaker: Ümmü Seleme
rows.claim: Umm Salama relates that Subayʿa's husband was killed while she was pregnant, she delivered forty nights later, and the Prophet allowed her to marry.
rows.anchor: Ümmü Seleme Hazretleri de dedi ki

rows.speaker: Ümmü Seleme
rows.claim: A second report says Subayʿa sought the Prophet's ruling after delivering soon after her husband's death, and he instructed her that she could marry.
rows.anchor: Sübey‘atü’l-Eslemiyye zevcinin vefâtından biraz sonra vaz‘-ı haml etti, Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem’den istiftâ eyledi

rows.speaker: Sübey‘a binti’l-Hâris
rows.claim: Subayʿa says her husband Saʿd b. Khawla died during the Farewell Pilgrimage; she delivered before four months and ten days, then the Prophet ruled her lawful upon delivery despite Abu al-Sanabil's objection.
rows.anchor: zevcinin vefâtından dört ay on gün geçmeden evvel doğurduğunu ve nifâsından kalktığında Benî Abdüddâr’dan bir zat olan Ebu’s-Senâbil
